parts.title: Leaving Home
parts.text: Mirela pressed her forehead to the airplane window and gripped the little wooden bird her grandmother had carved. She would **cherish** it forever, since it was all she could carry from the old kitchen. Her family was leaving to find **refuge** from years of hardship. A kind church group had agreed to **sponsor** them, helping with rent and paperwork for a year. Soon they would **resettle** in a city she had only seen in photographs.

parts.title: The Crowded Hallway
parts.text: On her first morning at the new school, the hallway was **bustling**, and Mirela felt like a tiny boat in a rushing river. She was already **homesick**, missing the smell of her mother's bread. A girl named Sofia greeted her with a wide smile, but Mirela, a **newcomer** who knew only ten English words, froze. Then a boy named Tunde stepped forward. He had lived in her homeland for two years, and he offered to be her **interpreter**. Suddenly the day felt less frightening.

parts.title: Finding a Place
parts.text: Learning English was hard, but Mirela decided to **overcome** each challenge one word at a time. Her teacher explained that **assimilation** did not mean forgetting your past; it meant adding new customs without losing the old ones. Mirela's **aspiration** was to become a doctor who could talk with families in their own languages. At the winter festival, she shared her grandmother's bread recipe, and the class lined up for seconds. At last she felt a true sense of **belonging**.

parts.title: The Wooden Bird
parts.text: That night, Mirela set the carved bird on her windowsill beside a card signed by every classmate. Two homes and two languages felt like a bigger family, not a puzzle.
